title: Cigar end rot on Banana - Kenya

Header: Cigar end rot on Banana - Kenya

Prevention: De-sucker banana stools to maintain 3-4 plants per stool.
Prune banana plants and shade trees to reduce humidity which may create favourable conditions for disease development.
Remove floral remains on the tip of fingers manually 8-11 days after bunch formation.
Remove the male bud 15cm (half feet) below the last hand (when the fingers have folded in).
Harvest at maturity to reduce susceptibility to the disease.
Store in a cool dry place to reduce the incidences of the disease.
Minimise bruising of the fruits during harvesting and transportation.
Advanced damage showing greyish ash cigar end on banana fingers. (Source:
Monitoring: Look for dry rot/ black necrosis spread from the flower into the tip of immature fingers with an ashy grey appearance, looking like a cigar end.
Take action when the first infestation is noticed.
Direct Control: Remove collapsing, dying and dead leaves and burn to reduce inoculum levels.
Remove and bury infected fingers to prevent the spread of fungus.
Do not empty pesticides into drains.
Spray affected banana bunches with thiophanate-methyl-based products.
Spray affected banana bunches with propineb-based products.
Restrictions: PCPB for target crops and pests.
Before use, read and follow pesticide product label instructions e.g., PHI, REI, usage and disposal of pesticide waste.
Always seek technical assistance before use of pesticide.
No synthetic chemicals registered against banana cigar end rot.
However, effective chemicals registered against fungal diseases on other food crops may be used with caution.
